title: Factorial Trailing Zeroes
statement: Return the number of trailing zeroes in n!. Do not compute n!.
hints: A trailing zero is a factor of 10, which is 2 * 5.
Factorials contain more twos than fives, so the number of fives is the answer.
Count floor(n/5) + floor(n/25) + floor(n/125) + ... because multiples of 25 contribute extra fives.

approaches.name: Compute n!
approaches.explanation: Possible in Python and the wrong lesson.

editorial: Every pair of a factor 2 and a factor 5 makes a trailing zero, and the fives are rarer. floor(n/5) counts multiples of 5, but 25 contributes two fives and was only counted once, so add floor(n/25), then floor(n/125), and so on. The loop divides n by 5 until it becomes zero.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def trailing_zeroes(n: int) -> int:
    zeros = 0
    while n:
        n //= 5
        zeros += n
    return zeros
